title: Technology Sector Update for 06/29/2018: DOMO,SAIC,RMBS

Technology stocks were backing away from their earlier session highs Friday afternoon, although shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 still were adding almost 0.5% in value in recent trading while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a nearly 0.8% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Domo Inc ( DOMO ) was sharply higher in its market debut, with shares of the freshly minted data analytics company Friday climbing almost 26% to a session high of $26.38 each on the Nasdaq Global Select market after overnight pricing its $193 million initial public offering of 9.2 million shares at $21 apiece with an expected $19 to $22 per share range. Domo also issued a 30-day option to underwriters to buy up to 1.38 million additonal shares to cover overallotments. After paying underwriter discounts and other offering expenses, Domo is expecting to receive around $174.7 million in net proceeds, rising to $201 million if the underwriters fully exercise their overallotment option and is planning to use the new capital for general corporate purposes, including investing in developing new technology to support its growth.
In other sector news:
+ Science Applications International ( SAIC ) was hanging on to a slim gain Friday afternoon, after late Thursday receiving a new Pentagon contract with a potential value of up to $116.2 million. The new three-year contract calls on the the technology consultants to provide sustainment support of integrated afloat and ashore tactical networks for the US Department of Defense. It also includes one two-year option period which, if exercised, could lift the overall value of the contract to around $196.5 million.
- Rambus ( RMBS ) fell as much as 3% on Friday after the semiconductor components company late Friday said it has fired chief executive Ron Black, effective immediately, and named general manager Luc Seraphin to take his place on an interim basis. In a statement, the company said the termination follows an incident unrelated to its financial and business performance although his conduct nevertheless fell short of the company standards. The Rambus board has started a formal search process to identify a successor.
